chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from his father, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send a Prophet except that with him was the fragrance of the quince.

key_terms.السَّفَرْجَلِ: Quince, a fruit known for its pleasant scent

ai.seo_question: What fragrance was present with every Prophet sent by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the divine perfection (kamal) inherent in all prophets, suggesting that the fragrance of quince served as a tangible sign of their prophethood to distinguish them from ordinary humans. In Shia scholarly tradition, this physical attribute is often interpreted as a manifestation of their spiritual purity and the subtle scent of their divine mission, reinforcing the concept of 'Fitrah' (innate nature) shared by all messengers.
